title: POC weekly sync - model flagging and fallback agreement
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's model comparison metrics, agree on pinning strategy, and finalize fallback rules for production pilot. Decided to pin to rdx-13b-q4 for higher-safety queries with a soft fallback to rdx-7b-quant for cost-sensitive paths; agreed to run targeted latency benchmarks and surface SSO/KMS requirements for Private deployment evaluation.
topics: Security: VPC peering, KMS, SOC2 evidence
Next steps: benchmarks, prompt set, pricing

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO - HelixHealth), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Evan (SRE), Sofia (PM)
Links referenced: pricing spreadsheet (Link: https://redwood.example/pricing/HELI), prompt set doc (internal), preliminary benchmark sheet (Link: https://redwood.example/bench/HELI)

Optional summary block: quick recap of last week - run of A/B on rdx-13b against rdx-7b-quant showed similar safety but cost delta; agreed to validate latency under realistic prefix caching.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes so we'll try to hit the bench results, model pin rec, and then security asks. Quick - is this still the right agenda?
[00:32] Liam: Yep, that's fine. Also gotta flag procurement timeline — we need a legal touchpoint by mid-May if we're going for Dedicated later.
[01:05] Maya: Noted. Jonah, do you wanna kick off with the benchmark highlights?
[01:22] Jonah: Sure. Uh, so we re-ran the evals on the 50 prompts Priya shared. There are two buckets: general clinical summarization and safety sensitive Q&A. rdx-13b-q4 kept a slight lead on hallucination metrics in the safety set, like 4% fewer hallucinated facts. Cost per 1k tokens was about 2.3x of rdx-7b-quant.
[01:58] Priya: Can you clarify what "q4" stands for in your notes? Sometimes the team mixes the internal tags.
[02:10] Jonah: Yeah, rdx-13b-q4 is our 4-bit quantized variant with extra safety fine-tuning — it's a good middle ground for the 13B architecture. Sorry if the tag is confusing.
[02:36] Evan: And latency numbers? Our SLO is 200ms p95 for the interactive flows. How did these shape up?
[02:48] Jonah: Right. Local benchmarks show rdx-13b-q4 at about 180ms p95 on a dedicated A100-like GPU with Redwood Dedicated auto-batching tuned; rdx-7b-quant was around 95ms p95. But when you add network and our VPC peering emulation, end-to-end moved up — rdx-13b to ~230-260ms p95 depending on payload, rdx-7b to ~130-160ms. So rdx-13b slightly breaches your 200ms SLO in the worst-case.
[03:34] Liam: That's a problem for us on the main product path, users notice delays above 200ms. Any way to shave off tokens or use prefix caching?
[03:47] Jonah: Definitely. We can use KV prefix cache for repeated preamble and also enable continuous batching with a smaller batching window for interactive lanes. There's a tradeoff: caching helps cost and latency, but for very diverse prompts it's less effective.
[04:12] Priya: Our prompts are moderately repetitive for certain flows, like discharge summaries, but ad-hoc clinician queries are pretty varied.
[04:27] Sofia: So maybe pin the critical safety flows to rdx-13b and route high-volume low-latency ones to rdx-7b?
[04:38] Maya: That's what we'd call a pin + soft-fallback policy. Pin the safety label to the 13B, but have a fallback rule when latency is breached or capacity constrained to route to the cheaper 7B-quant. We can also do canary first.
[04:58] Liam: I like that but concerned about semantic regression when switching models. We don't want content drift in summaries.
[05:12] Jonah: Agreed. We recommend shadow routing for the first week of canary: send the same inputs to both models but only serve responses from the primary. We'll collect quality metrics and if similarity stays above your threshold, then enable soft fallback.
[05:32] Priya: What's a realistic similarity threshold? We usually look for >=92% on rouge-like overlap for extracts, but that doesn't catch hallucinations.
[05:46] Jonah: We can add hallucination detectors and safety checks — your 10 safety-sensitive prompts will be gold for that. For openset similarity, we'd aim for 90-93% as a starting gating criteria.
[06:07] Evan: Operationally, if fallback happens, how will observability surface that? We need token-level cost and a flag in traces.
[06:18] Maya: Console will show per-route model breakdown with tagging for fallback events. We'll push an alert for increased fallback frequency. Token-level cost is in the console and can be exported.
[06:34] Liam: OK. What's the overhead of shadow traffic? Seems like double compute.
[06:45] Jonah: Yes, shadowing duplicates compute, so we recommend limited sampled shadowing, e.g., 5-10% of traffic to keep costs contained.
[06:58] Sofia: About Private deployment — we still need SOC2 docs and KMS flow. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[07:12] Maya: Yes, with Redwood Private we support KMS integration and HSM in some on-prem options. For VPC, we do VPC peering and private control plane options. We'll share the security packet and a KMS integration note after this meeting.
[07:31] Priya: Do you have any enterprise customers who did a similar pin+fallback pattern? Reference would help our stakeholders.
[07:41] Maya: We have a fintech and a telehealth customer who used the exact pattern; I'll include anonymized notes in the follow-up.
[07:52] Liam: Competitors? We looked at Bedrock but their routing is more manual and OpenAI's multi-model strategies are not as transparent on cost.
[08:05] Jonah: Also Anthropic's safety model is good but cost and latency tradeoffs were similar. We'll include a short competitor matrix in the follow-up.
[08:20] Priya: Back to model pinning: how do we freeze model versions so that a cloud-side model upgrade won't surprise us?
[08:31] Maya: You can pin exact model versions in the catalog — model IDs are immutable. We also support rollout policies: canary %, time windows, automatic rollback on metric regression.
[08:47] Evan: On rollback, how fast can you flip back in case production starts to degrade?
[08:56] Jonah: Typically under 2 minutes for a routing policy change; depends on caching TTLs and KV invalidation. We'll add an escape hatch button in the console flow.
[09:10] Sofia: Priya had a note earlier about safety-tuned prompts — can we do input classification to decide routing?
[09:21] Priya: Yes, we'd like a lightweight classifier to tag incoming requests as safety-sensitive, then route accordingly. We can host that classifier in our infra or use Redwood's route hooks.
[09:34] Jonah: Redwood supports pre-routing classifiers via a webhook or you can use a built-in model-based router. If you host your classifier, you control the logic and privacy; hooking into the route is straightforward.
[09:50] Liam: Any implications for SSO — we need SAML and SCIM for users.
[09:58] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll attach the SSO setup guide in the post-meeting note.
[10:08] Priya: Can we talk about the prompt set you used for bench? We need to see the variants and the prefixes.
[10:16] Jonah: Sure, the sheet shows 50 prompts with lengths varying 20-400 tokens. We tested with and without a 150-token preamble to emulate the patient context. The preamble changes token counts and latency substantially.
[10:34] Evan: On caching: if we cache the preamble, do you store patient data? That has implications for PHI.
[10:42] Maya: Important note — Redwood's KV cache can be configured to avoid storing PHI; you can use a hashed or tokenized preamble or choose not to cache PHI-laden prefixes. For Private deployments, you control storage policies.
[10:58] Liam: Good. Let's get more concrete — what's your recommended default policy here?
[11:05] Jonah: Recommend: 1) Pin safety-labeled routes to rdx-13b-q4. 2) Enable canary shadowing at 5% for 7 days. 3) Soft fallback to rdx-7b-quant when p95 latency > 220ms for more than 5 minutes or when capacity constraints trigger. 4) Collect quality metrics with hallucination detector and similarity score; rollback if similarity < 90% on safety set.
[11:36] Sofia: That seems reasonable but can we set a stricter p95 threshold of 200ms?
[11:44] Liam: We should try 200ms. If the 13B can't meet it reliably, we'll restrict 13B to batch/async flows only.
[11:55] Jonah: We can try to optimize kernels and batching but there is a cost floor. The 13B will likely need slightly more headroom. We'll run a more realistic end-to-end bench with your VPC emulation.
[12:10] Priya: On prompt engineering, we saw consistent differences in tone. That's a product UX thing — do we version prompts along with model pins?
[12:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports prompt sets tied to model pins so you can freeze both model and prompt versions together.
[12:30] Evan: For Dedicated capacity, what are minimum commit sizes?
[12:37] Maya: Depends on GPU family; for A100-class dedicated pools it's monthly committed vGPU hours — I'll include an options table in the pricing sheet.
[12:46] Sofia: Any quick wins to reduce 13B latency before we commit to Dedicated?
[12:52] Jonah: Light wins: reduce prefix length, enable KV caching (PHI aware), and tweak batching windows. Medium: tune kernel selection and sequence-length specific kernels—some of that's runtime-level and we'd need a short tuning window.
[13:08] Liam: OK. I want to make sure rollbacks don't affect audit logs and compliance.
[13:16] Maya: All rollouts, fallback events, and model switches are logged with user and token-level metadata and can be exported for audits. For Private we can also keep logs on-prem.
[13:30] Priya: Are you comfortable sharing the raw bench scripts so we can replicate?
[13:37] Jonah: Yes, we'll share the scripts and the dataset; we just need a non-PII sanitized copy.
[13:46] Sofia: Procurement wants an itemized cost model showing cost per 1k requests for both models including shadow cost.
[13:55] Maya: We'll add a shadow-cost line to the pricing sheet.
[14:02] Liam: Timeline - if we lock a pilot config this month, can we go live with a canary by mid-June?
[14:10] Jonah: That's feasible if benchmarks and security review complete by mid-May and procurement signs off. So roughly 4-6 weeks from canary planning to small live rollout.
[14:24] Priya: Quick question — when you say quantized 7B, are you using int8 or 4-bit?
[14:31] Jonah: The 7B-quant is an 8-bit optimized path; we also have a 4-bit variant but quality varies by workload. That's why the 13B-q4 is interesting — it's 4-bit but with extra safety tuning.
[14:48] Evan: On performance instrumentation — how do traces correlate with downstream DB writes? We need to see end-to-end latency.
[14:59] Maya: The console can ingest traces via OpenTelemetry and will show per-request spans including the DB write. We'll help wire that up in your staging environment.
[15:12] Liam: Can you remind us what happens if capacity is constrained — automatic fallback or queueing?
[15:21] Jonah: Policy based — you can choose queueing, fallback to cheaper model, or spill to a different region. We usually recommend fallback + alerting for critical user-facing paths.
[15:34] Sofia: Let's record the decisions from today so we can move forward.
[15:38] Maya: Decisions: pin safety flows to rdx-13b-q4; soft fallback to rdx-7b-quant on latency/capacity triggers; 5% shadowing during canary; run end-to-end bench with VPC emulation. We'll share docs.
[15:53] Priya: I'll upload the prompt CSV by Saturday and mark the safety ones.
[15:59] Jonah: Great — I'll take the bench action. Expect a rough latency/cost matrix by Monday.
[16:06] Liam: Procurement will need the SOC2/ISO artifacts and an initial T&C outline.
[16:13] Maya: We'll include the security packet and a procurement checklist in the follow-up.
[16:20] Evan: One last ops question — if we do Private deployment, will Redwood still host the control plane or can we self-host?
[16:28] Maya: You can opt for a private control plane with customer-managed networking; on-prem full self-host is available in certain engagements. We'll detail options.
[16:40] Sofia: OK, let's wrap and confirm next steps.
[16:45] Maya: Thanks everyone. Quick recap and owners: Jonah runs latency bench (due 2026-05-11), Maya shares pricing and competitor matrix (due 2026-05-08), Priya shares prompts (due 2026-05-09), Evan confirms VPC details (due 2026-05-10), Sofia schedules security review (due 2026-05-14). We'll meet next Wednesday same time to review results — tentatively 2026-05-13.
[17:18] Liam: Sounds good, thanks.
[17:23] Priya: Thanks all.
[17:26] Maya: Bye everyone.

End of transcript.
